title.rendered: Come to Me, All Who Are Weary: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Come to me, all who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” A morning devotional for anyone tired down to the soul.

content.rendered:
You know the feeling. The alarm at 5:30 AM. The commute you have made a thousand times. The inbox that never empties. The weight of expectations you carry from the moment your feet hit the floor. Jesus is talking to you in Matthew 11:28.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, September 14, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”
Matthew 11:28-30 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

You know the feeling. The alarm at five thirty in the morning. The commute you have made a thousand times. The inbox that never empties. The bills that never stop arriving. The children who need you. The parents who need you. The work that needs you. The weight of expectations you carry from the moment your feet hit the floor to the moment you fall exhausted into bed. In an average week in the modern world, a working adult is exhausted before Wednesday. This is the ordinary condition of ordinary life. And Jesus, two thousand years before smartphones and open-plan offices and back-to-back meetings, was talking to you in Matthew 11:28.

“Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” The Greek word for “labor” is kopiaō, the word for physical, sweat-of-the-brow exhaustion. The word for “heavy laden” is phortizō, meaning to be loaded down like a beast of burden with a weight that is more than the body was designed to carry. Jesus is not speaking to the leisured. He is speaking to the ones who are already tired. Already stretched. Already carrying more than they can hold. And His invitation is not “try harder.” His invitation is “come to Me.” And the promise attached is not a productivity hack. It is rest.

The Passion Translation opens up the tenderness of the invitation: “Are you weary, carrying a heavy burden? Then come to me. I will refresh your life, for I am your oasis. Simply join your life with mine. Learn my ways and you’ll discover that I’m gentle, humble, easy to please. You will find refreshment and rest in me. For all that I require of you will be pleasant and easy to bear” (Matthew 11:28-30 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy-laden and overburdened, and I will cause you to rest. [I will ease and relieve and refresh your souls]” (Matthew 11:28 AMPC). Ease. Relieve. Refresh. Not later. Now, if you come.

The most important verb in the passage is the first one. Come. The rest is on offer. It is not a rest that comes automatically because you are a Christian. It is a rest that comes when you actively bring your weariness to Jesus. Many exhausted believers stay exhausted because they never actually come. They keep trying to carry the load themselves, and pray for strength between meetings, and hope God will multiply their hours. Jesus is not offering to multiply your hours. He is offering to take your yoke. There is a difference. His yoke is easy. His burden is light. The rabbi’s teaching, in first-century Judea, was called a rabbi’s “yoke.” Every rabbi’s yoke was heavy in some way. Every rabbi’s yoke had rules and expectations. Only one Rabbi ever said, “Take My yoke upon you and you will find rest for your souls.” His teaching does not add weight. It removes weight.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is one of the most important invitations Jesus ever gave. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if you have been carrying a weight for so long that you have forgotten what it feels like to put it down, come to Him. Actually come. Not once at conversion and never again. Today. In this hour. Bring the tiredness. Bring the load. Bring the exhaustion the world does not see. He is gentle and lowly in heart. His yoke is easy. His burden is light. And He will give you the rest your soul has been longing for. That is His promise, and He keeps every one of them.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus invites me to come to Him with my weariness, not to hide it or push through it in my own strength. Today I come. I bring the load I have been carrying. I bring the exhaustion the world does not see. I take His yoke and I lay down mine. I learn from Him. And I trust the promise. My soul finds rest in the One who is gentle and lowly in heart. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I come to Jesus today with my weariness. I take His yoke. I lay down mine. His yoke is easy. His burden is light. My soul finds rest in Him.
